name: Licking County

actions.title: Intel Mega-Campus Utility & Infrastructure Agreements
actions.summary: Licking County and New Albany/Columbus-area jurisdictions approved extensive utility, road, and service agreements to support Intel's $20 billion+ semiconductor and data-center-adjacent campus, including water and sewer capacity expansions managed at the county level.

actions.title: Intel Campus Tax Incentive (Enterprise Zone) Approval
actions.summary: Licking County commissioners approved enterprise zone tax exemptions tied to Intel's Ohio One campus, one of the largest such incentive packages in Ohio history, covering thousands of acres of industrial and data-infrastructure land.

contextBlurb: Licking County has become one of the nation's most active data-center and semiconductor investment corridors, anchored by Intel's massive Ohio One campus near New Albany. The county has approved sweeping infrastructure and tax-incentive packages to accommodate enormous energy, water, and land demands. Community debates have emerged around water supply adequacy, traffic, and the pace of agricultural land conversion.

name: Franklin County

actions.title: (City of Columbus) Data Center Zoning & Tax-Abatement Reviews
actions.summary: The City of Columbus, within Franklin County, approved multiple data-center development zoning amendments and tax-abatement agreements, drawing scrutiny from city council members over the low job-creation-to-incentive ratio typical of hyperscale data centers.

actions.title: (City of Columbus) AEP Ohio Grid Capacity Study for Data Center Load Growth
actions.summary: AEP Ohio, serving Franklin County and Columbus, initiated formal grid-capacity studies after data center electricity demand surges threatened to strain the regional transmission system, prompting local utility coordination discussions with Columbus city officials.

contextBlurb: Franklin County and the City of Columbus sit at the center of Ohio's data-center boom, with hyperscale operators attracted by AEP Ohio's power infrastructure and the state's favorable business climate. City council debates have focused on whether tax abatements for low-employment data centers represent good public policy. Rapid load growth is prompting grid reliability reviews by AEP Ohio.

name: Delaware County

actions.title: Data Center Siting & Zoning Amendments in Powell/Lewis Center Corridor
actions.summary: Delaware County townships amended zoning codes to accommodate a wave of data-center proposals along the US-23 and SR-750 corridors, with commissioners approving conditional-use permits for multiple large-scale facilities while residents raised concerns about noise, traffic, and land use.

contextBlurb: Delaware County, immediately north of Columbus, has experienced rapid data-center siting interest due to its proximity to the Intel campus corridor and available land. Township trustees and county planners have been updating zoning regulations to manage noise, setbacks, and utility demands. Residents near proposed sites have organized opposition citing noise and disruption to rural character.
